reviews.review: I am a DRG greybeard who really wanted to like this but would not recommend it in it's current form. I think there's a good base to build on eventually, and the studio has a long history of being good to their gamers, but this currently misses the mark for me. The 5 classes have very little identity since they all share the same weapons and upgrades, there are far too many damage types (>11), beers are governed by a cheesy QTE instead of collecting supplies in game, it's impossible to tell if a card will actually affect your build/damage, etc.

It's obviously not DRG 2.0 (it was never meant to be).
It's obviously not an expansion. It's a reduction/shrinkage.
This leaves us with a Spinoff I guess. Something is indeed "off" with this Spin.

BORING GAMEPLAY LOOP
It's baseline DRG with a Twist. The whole game is just long Deep Dives consisting of [strike] Morkite [/strike] Expenite Mining Missions with some annoying bosses as a reward at the end. 

The game is extremely formulaic and the joy of cave exploration is gone. Every cavern feels the same and every mission feels the same. Drop down, rush to find the Bio-booster and the Workbench, mine a bit of Expenite, fight one or two core-spawn hordes, hit the elevator button... and repeat three to seven times. If you are lucky there might be some Bonus Events spawned or if you are extraordinarily lucky there might be DRG Drones and Geodes. That's it. The Devs will probably add more variety but the core loop of "Expenite Mining Missions only" needs to be expanded.

UNINSPIRED ENEMIES
The Glyphids in the main game were fun looking bugs. Fun to fight, fun to shoot, fun to gib. Slamming with a drop pod into this alien ecosystem to burn, loot and pillage the nature (living and unliving) was fun.

Core-spawn on the other hand? Abstract demons/mutants who look like they crawled out of Metro 2033. Spawning from portals in the cave walls for whatever reason?! What is this - Faerun/Golarion meets DRG?

Lore-wise we are deeper, sure. Rogue Core magic shennanigans probably ruined the local wildlife (except the Leeches of course, how fun)... as a result the caves feel even emptier.

UNINSPIRED ROGUE-LITE ELEMENTS
Artifact-tier upgrades feel good, but the rest is uninspired, boring percentual increases (20 % more damage, +12 armor, +20 HP) or "Do X elemental damage on Winter Solstice"

Upgrades that make enemies drop Red Sugar on XYZ condition are mandatory for bullet-spongy, lengthy, annoying boss-fights (multiple boss invincibility phases).

WEAPONS
To end on a positive note - The weapons feel fun most of the time. Both the old and the new weapons. I just wish the new weapons were added to the main game.

Some weapon upgrades are straight up unusable though. 
Few examples:
Double barrel shotgun with a salvo - avoid this like Smallpox - uncontrollable recoil and a waste of ammo
Hurricane with a salvo - avoid this like the Bubonic plague - words cannot describe how bad it is
Plasma rifle with auto-aim - avoid this like the Plague of Justinian - it never shoots where you want it to

PERSONAL NOTE
I enjoy playing this with friends. In the same sense watching the paint dry would be more fun with friends. I would never play this on my own.

I want to preface this with a 'certainly needs way more time in the oven', but even now it's still enjoyable. My main gripe is that for solo, Cautious feels mandatory, and you have some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths here and there. I do have to say though, that my main gripe is the lack of real synergy between upgrades, or just a general lack of scaling for the most part. Combining upgrades that make red sugar drop, with better healing from red sugar, an the elemental combo of poison and fire to make repeated bursts of fire are the only real pieces of synergy I've seen.
I still recommend the game, it's fun and has amazing gunplay, especially now with the higher focus on being precise to get things done making a well aimed shot all the more satisfying. In addition, one of the classes, along with crit upgrades, and possibly stacking loads of crit chance, can allow for multicrit, which feels incredibly satisfying and was a joy to see properly implemented. The other classes have fun gimmicks, too. The rewind of Retcon feels enjoyable. The drone also feels good to just release as. The Slicer has incredible crowd control up close, and Guardian is an okay tank, and is the only one that doesn't feel super great to me. I think this'll end up being something great with time.
Super fun and very polished for early access

I can't in good faith recommend this game. As an avid roguelike obsessive and someone with hundreds of hours in DRG, I was incredibly excited for this game. Initial reviews weren't great so I waited until after the first big patch. This game is insanely hard, but it never feels like its hard in a way that I can improve on. Even on the lowest "cautious" difficulty, i am running out of ammo on the 2nd or 3rd floor, in the midst of 5+ minutes of pure combat, and then i hear a "swarm incoming"  message as I watch my corpse be danced on by 30+ enemies after i just killed over a hundred. There is no time for exploration, not enough ammo, and an incredible array of "feel bad" mechanics that make me want to play less with each inevitable and horrific loss. I have watched videos to see what I'm missing, but it seems I'm already using the "meta builds" which are still outright useless if your weapon isn't exactly perfect. Very rarely do I die and feel that I had any opportunity to survive. This game genuinely feels like it's punishing me for playing, and the upsides of the exceedingly rare victory are entirely negligible.

I may pick this game up again in the future, but for now it'll be back to DRG until this game actually is balanced and enjoyable. I don't expect Danger 1 levels of ease, but I DO expect to feel like a loss is something I could have possibly prevented.
